cpu_timeout_policy._doc: Per-step cpu_timeout is a CPU-second runaway catcher complementing the wall 'timeout'. CPU-seconds are width-invariant (fixed work regardless of -j) and load-independent (a blocked step accrues ~0 CPU), so one budget is correct on any machine. Enforced by the Python safe-ci-dag-runner scheduler (polls cgroup cpu.stat usage_usec at 1Hz, reaps on breach); the Rust engine round-trips it schema-only. Both engines ignore this block and per-node cpu_timeout_basis as unknown keys.
cpu_timeout_policy.cpu_per_wall_rationale: cpu-bound=3 anchored on the one measured DAG compile ratio (build.workspace ~919 raw max cpu_s / 360s est ~= 2.55, rounded up). light/latency-bound=1: wall-bound work accrues ~1 cpu-s per wall-s. For cpu-bound nodes the 9x-est budget can exceed the wall 'timeout' BY DESIGN: a multi-core runaway burns cpu-seconds ~N times faster than wall-seconds, so the budget trips fast under parallelism (a 32-core clippy spin hits 2700 cpu_s in ~85s wall) while single-core spins are caught by the wall timeout. Generous by intent: a runaway-catcher is asymmetric -- catching a hang late beats never catching it.
cpu_timeout_policy.measured_override: Where >=5 real samples exist, a measured budget = round(1.5 * max_observed_cpu_s) WINS over the formula. Current agent-env samples are inflated => fail-safe-loose (acceptable for a catcher). Node basis strings mark which rule set each value.

excluded.build.dbi_release: Left bare intentionally: OOM premise (peak==cap) refuted -- 5.03 GiB aggregate vs 8 GiB cap; fails a portable manifest gate in ~55s, not an OOM. Owned by hermit-lander. Add a budget only with a real >=5-sample measurement.
